name: Yufeng (Kevin) Chen
title: NBX Career Development Professor; Associate Professor; Soft and Micro Robotics Laboratory director
fitReason: Strong specialized overlap: neural policies trained from robust MPC and PPO-based policies directly control insect-scale physical robots; attractive for algorithm–hardware co-design rather than general-purpose manipulation.

physicalEvidence.summary: The August 2025 preprint, published in Science Advances December 3, 2025, verifies imitation-learned robust tube MPC on a 750 mg flapping-wing robot, including repeated turns and ten flips in eleven seconds. It uses external Vicon sensing, offboard computation and a power tether; this is not untethered onboard autonomy. A separate RoboSoft 2025 paper deploys behavior-cloned/PPO policies on two physical soft-actuated micro-flyers. February 2026 work demonstrates onboard sensing/computation in a 1.29 g robot with human high-level commands; it supports current hardware activity, not a claim that the earlier learned controller became onboard or power-autonomous.

shortVisit.summary: The current lab opportunities page says it is not searching for visiting students because of limited funding, but explicitly welcomes discussions with visiting students who have external fellowships. This is a conditional, duration-unspecified inquiry exception. The one-year project preference appears in the currently enrolled MIT-student section; its applicability to external visitors is not established.

scoreReasons.fit: Both imitation learning and PPO-based control execute on physical robots, with explicit robust-control interaction.
scoreReasons.physical: Own MIT lab co-leads named physical micro-flyers and current February 2026 experiments; external sensing, computation and power limitations preserved.
scoreReasons.shortVisit: Five points only for the explicit externally fellowship-funded visitor inquiry exception; no duration or 2027 commitment.
scoreReasons.freshness: Current faculty/lab pages, April 2026 institutional seminar and February 2026 primary hardware paper; neural-flight experiments correctly dated2025.
